critical_code_review_comments: orders.py save_templates(): only whitelists keys present in DEFAULT_TEMPLATES; unknown keys sent by client are silently dropped. Fine, but consider returning 400 for unknown keys to give admin explicit feedback.

orders.py render_template(): substitutes with simple str.replace(); if a customer name contains '{order}'-like text it will be replaced again on next pass. Currently the loop only runs once per placeholder so acceptable; a safer approach is str.format_map with a defaultdict to avoid injection edge cases.
orders.py dispatch_register(): uses date_from/date_to inclusive on dispatch.dispatch_date string comparison (YYYY-MM-DD), which works because ISO date sorts lexicographically — fine.
pricing.py set_product_pricing(): silently 'continue' if variant_id missing or category not in CATEGORIES. Consider returning 400 on invalid input so admin sees typos.

AdminProducts.jsx persistPricing(): posts every offer sequentially in an await loop; for many offers this can be slow. Consider Promise.all for parallel offer creation. Also, no rollback if PUT /pricing/product succeeds but POST /offers fails — could leave partial state.

AdminProducts.jsx: after editing/saving, on-error state does not close dialog nor reset saving flag if persistPricing throws mid-way (caught, saving reset OK). Verified: 'Product & pricing saved' toast displayed on success.

AdminDispatchList.jsx: uses Radix Select with SelectItem value='all'; if response's transports list contains 'Customer Pickup' it will render TWICE (once from data.transports, once hardcoded). Minor duplicate risk.
